correctness.rationale: Every signed lift in the defining rate sum contributes to the eigenvalue 2κF_p(2πm/N); lifts divisible by N contribute zero. The nearest-neighbor term makes all modes except m=0 positive. Differentiation and the Laplace/geometric summation are justified by absolute summability of r^(1−p) for p>2, and the resulting integrand has the sign of sin θ. Reflection and strict increase on (0,π) give exactly the stated minimizers, including N=3. At p=3 the twice-differentiated cosine series converges locally uniformly off multiples of 2π by Dirichlet's test; the logarithmic identity gives −log θ+O(θ²) near zero. Integrating twice from zero with F₃(0)=F₃'(0)=0 gives (θ²/2)log(1/θ)+3θ²/4+O(θ⁴). For ε=z/log N and θ=2π/N, the Taylor error for r≤N is bounded by Cκθ⁴ times the sum of r^(1−ε), and the r>N contribution by 4κ times the tail of r^(−3−ε). Both are O_K(κN^(−2)) because N^(−ε)=e^(−z) is bounded on K. The remaining decreasing sum differs from its integral by O(1), and that integral is log N times Φ(z) with continuous value at zero. Reciprocals give the stated spectral times; a squared deviation has rate twice the gap as a worst-case rate or when a gap mode is present, and can decay faster for other initial data. This is not a finite-dephasing quantum statement. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: In (25.12.11), set s=p−1 and w=e^(iθ); the imaginary part of w/(e^t−w) is positive for 0<θ<π, so F'_p>0 and the minimum among nonzero sampled angles is the first reflected pair.

In (25.12.12), put p=3+ε and w=e^(iθ). After taking real parts the order-θ² contribution to ζ(p)−Re Li_p(w) is θ²[ζ(1+ε)/2+Γ(−2−ε)cos(πε/2)θ^ε]. Higher even powers are O(θ⁴) locally uniformly in ε, by normal convergence of the remaining series for |θ|<2π. Laurent expansion gives θ²[(1−θ^ε)/(2ε)+O_K(1)] when ε=z/log N and θ=2π/N. The divided difference equals (log N)Φ(z) plus O_K(1) after restoring the factor 1/2, i.e. (1−θ^ε)/(2ε)=(log N)Φ(z)/2+O_K(1), uniformly including ε=0 by continuity.
At ε=0 the same Laurent cancellation leaves (1/2)log(1/θ)+3/4 inside the brackets, with the uniform O(θ⁴) remainder; Catalano's S30 independently prints the corresponding two terms for A(0)−A(θ).

value.rationale: As a statement about this specified rate generator, the asymptotic gives a physically interpretable normalization and predicts the change of relaxation across a size-dependent range of exponents. It cleanly separates gap time from squared-deviation time and finite rate-periodization from quantum or open-boundary dynamics. This usefulness does not make a direct implication of classical formulas an independent original finding.
